subject: math
title: Angles and Rectangles: Right, Acute, Obtuse and Straight Angles, Parallel and Perpendicular Sides
seo_title: Grade 4 Angles Worksheets: Acute, Obtuse, Parallel and Perpendicular (Free, Ontario Math)
standard_text: Identify angles and classify them as right, straight, acute, or obtuse
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on angles and rectangles for the Ontario curriculum: compare angles with a right angle, classify right, straight, acute and obtuse angles, find angles in clocks and shapes, spot parallel and perpendicular sides, and find lines of symmetry. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Compare every angle with a right angle: less is acute, more is obtuse, 2 right angles is straight.
key_sub: A rectangle has 4 right angles, 2 pairs of parallel sides and 2 lines of symmetry (a square has 4). The size of an angle is how wide it opens, not the length of its arms.
body_html:
Compare every angle with a right angle

An angle is made by two arms that meet at a point. A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. Put the corner of the paper on the angle to compare.

Four kinds of angles

NameCompared with a right angle
Acute angleless than a right angle
Right angleexactly a square corner (the small square shows it)
Obtuse anglegreater than a right angle, less than a straight angle
Straight angle2 right angles: the arms make a straight line
Example

At 4 o’clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?

A right angle is 3 hour marks (3 o’clock) and a straight angle is 6 (6 o’clock). 4 is between them.

Answer: an obtuse angle

The length of the arms does not matter. These two angles are the same size.

Parallel and perpendicular

Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, like train rails. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, like the edges at the corner of a page.

Rectangles and squares

A rectangle has 4 right angles. Its opposite sides are parallel, and sides that meet at a corner are perpendicular. A square is a rectangle with 4 equal sides.

Example

Is the diagonal of a rectangle 12 cm long and 6 cm wide a line of symmetry?

Fold on the diagonal: the corners stick out past each other, so the halves do not match.

Answer: no (only a square’s diagonals are lines of symmetry)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleLook at how wide the angle opens, not the arm length
Thinking a tilted right angle is not a right angleTurning an angle does not change its size or name
Saying a straight line is “no angle”Two arms in a straight line make a straight angle: 2 right angles
Calling lines parallel because they do not touch yetParallel lines stay the same distance apart all the way
Counting the diagonals of a rectangle as lines of symmetryFold to check: a rectangle has 2 lines, a square has 4

faq.q: What angles do Grade 4 students learn in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Grade 4 students identify right, straight, acute and obtuse angles by comparing them with a right angle. Measuring angles in degrees with a protractor comes in Grade 5.

faq.q: How can my child check if an angle is a right angle at home?
faq.a: Use the corner of a sheet of paper or a book. If the angle fits the corner exactly, it is a right angle; if it fits inside, it is acute; if it opens wider, it is obtuse.

faq.q: What is the difference between parallel and perpendicular lines?
faq.a: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet. Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle.

faq.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle have?
faq.a: A rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry, through the middles of opposite sides. A square has 4, because its diagonals are lines of symmetry too.

sets.title: Compare angles with a right angle

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm is inside the paper corner. The angle is smaller than the corner, so it is less than a right angle.
The second arm is far outside the paper corner, but the arms do not make a straight line. The angle is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Which of these has a corner that is a right angle?
c: the point of a slice of pizza cut into 8
the tip of a sharp pencil
a book lying open and flat
items.e: The corner of a page is a square corner: a right angle. A pencil tip and a pizza slice tip are narrower (acute), and a book lying flat makes a straight angle.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm lies along the edge of the paper. A tilted angle can still be a right angle.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm is inside the paper corner, so the angle is less than a right angle.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm is outside the paper corner, so the angle is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Liam draws two angles. Angle P has arms 10 cm long and angle Q has arms 3 cm long. He says angle P must be larger. Is he right?
c: No, arm length does not change the size of an angle
Yes, longer arms make a larger angle
No, angle Q is always larger
Yes, angle P is 7 cm larger
items.e: The size of an angle is how wide it opens between the arms. You cannot tell which is larger from the arm lengths.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm is well inside the paper corner, so the angle is less than a right angle.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm lies exactly along the edge of the paper. The angle fits the corner, so it is equal to a right angle.

items.q: Put the angles in order from smallest to largest.
items.e: Y is less than a right angle, Z is a right angle and X is greater than a right angle. Look at the opening, not the arm length.
C is narrower than a square corner. A is greater than a right angle, B is a right angle and D is a straight angle.

items.q: The corner of a sheet of paper is placed on the angle. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The second arm is outside the paper corner. The angle opens wider than the corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle is equal to a right angle?
items.e: C is a square corner: the small square shows it. It is tilted and has short arms, but it is still a right angle. A and D are less, and B is greater.
Angle P is greater than a right angle and angle Q is less. Long arms do not make an angle larger.

items.q: Leah puts the corner of a sheet of paper on an angle. The angle fits inside the corner and there is space left over. How does the angle compare with a right angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than the paper corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both are right angles (the small squares show it). Tilting an angle or making its arms longer does not change it.

items.q: Jayden folds a scrap of paper in half. Then he folds it in half again, so the folded edge lies on top of itself. What angle does the new folded corner make?
items.e: The first fold makes a straight edge: a straight angle. Folding it in half splits the straight angle into 2 equal parts. Half of a straight angle is a right angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Both angles open the same amount. Only the arms are different lengths, and arm length does not change an angle.

items.q: Which marked angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is greater than a right angle and angle P is less. Q is larger, even though its arms are shorter.

items.q: Which angle is greater than a right angle?
items.e: B opens wider than a square corner. A and D are less than a right angle and C is a right angle. B has the shortest arms, but arm length does not matter.

sets.title: Right, straight, acute and obtuse angles

items.q: An angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: Between a right angle and a straight angle is an obtuse angle.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
items.e: Acute is less than a right angle. Obtuse is between a right angle and a straight angle, and a straight angle is 2 right angles.
A straight angle is 2 right angles. The two arms make a straight line. Turning the angle does not change its name.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle: narrower than the corner of a sheet of paper.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked?
items.e: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its name.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle: narrower than the corner of a sheet of paper.
A straight angle is 2 right angles. The two arms make a straight line.

items.q: Which angle is a square corner, exactly a quarter turn?
items.e: A right angle is a square corner. It is a quarter of a full turn.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked?
items.e: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a sheet of paper. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its name.

items.q: How many right angles make a straight angle?
items.e: Put 2 square corners side by side. Together their outside arms make a straight line.

items.q: What kind of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle: narrower than the corner of a sheet of paper.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.
C is the only angle less than a right angle. A and D are obtuse and B is a right angle.
An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle but less than a straight angle.

items.q: Arjun says this is not a right angle because it is tilted. Is he right?
c: Yes, it is an acute angle
Yes, right angles must have a flat arm
No, it is a right angle
Yes, it is an obtuse angle
items.e: The small square shows a square corner. Turning an angle does not change its size or its name.

c: No, it is a right angle
No, it is an obtuse angle
Yes, a straight line is not an angle
No, it is a straight angle
items.e: The two arms meet at the dot and point in opposite directions. That is an angle: a straight angle (2 right angles).
In D the two arms make a straight line. A is obtuse: close to a straight angle, but less.

items.q: An angle is less than a right angle. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: An acute angle is less than a right angle. An obtuse angle is greater than a right angle.

items.q: The two arms of an angle make a straight line. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: When the arms point in opposite directions and make a straight line, the angle is a straight angle.

sets.title: Angles in shapes and real life (clock hands)

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point in opposite directions. They make a straight line: a straight angle.

items.q: This door is seen from above. It opened from the dashed line. What kind of angle has it opened?
items.e: The door has opened past a square corner but not to a straight line, so the angle is obtuse.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands make a square corner: a right angle.

items.q: Which angle in this triangle is a right angle?
items.e: Angle A is a square corner: one arm goes straight across and the other goes straight up. B and C are acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: The hands are 4 hour marks apart. That is more than 3 (a right angle) and less than 6 (a straight angle): obtuse.
Each corner of this hexagon is wider than a square corner but less than a straight line: obtuse.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. What kind of angle is at the tip of each slice?
items.e: 4 equal slices fit round the centre. Each one is a quarter turn: a right angle.

items.q: Amira opens a book and lays it flat on the table. What angle do the two covers make?
items.e: When the book lies flat, the covers make a straight line: a straight angle.

items.q: What kind of angle do the blades of these scissors make?
items.e: The blades open less than a square corner, so the angle is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: The hands are 2 hour marks apart. A right angle is 3 hour marks (like 3 o’clock), so this is less: acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: From 12 to 5 is 5 hour marks: more than 3 (a right angle) but less than 6 (a straight angle). The angle is obtuse.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The two corners on the left side are square corners. The top right corner is obtuse and the bottom right corner is acute.

items.q: Which angle in this triangle is obtuse?
items.e: Angle C at the top opens wider than a right angle, so it is obtuse. A and B are acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: From 10 to 12 is only 2 hour marks, less than 3. The angle is acute.

items.q: This door is seen from above. It opened from the dashed line. What kind of angle has it opened?
items.e: The door has opened less than a square corner, so the angle is acute.

items.q: How many right angles does this house shape have?
items.e: The 2 corners at the bottom, where the walls meet the floor, are right angles. The 3 corners of the roof are obtuse.

items.q: What kind of angle do the clock hands make?
items.e: From 9 to 12 is 3 hour marks, the same as 12 to 3. The hands make a square corner: a right angle.
The screen leans back past a square corner, but it is not flat. That is an obtuse angle.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. What kind of angle is at the tip of one slice?
items.e: 2 slices make a quarter of the pizza: a right angle. One slice is half of that, so it is acute.

items.q: At which time do the hands of an analog clock make a straight angle?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 6, the opposite way. At 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock the hands make right angles.

items.q: Which pair is parallel?
c: the two rails of a train track
the two hands of a clock at 3 o’clock
the two blades of open scissors
a flagpole and the flat ground
items.e: Train rails stay the same distance apart so the wheels fit. The clock hands at 3 o’clock and the flagpole and ground are perpendicular.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, which side is parallel to side AB?
items.e: Side AB is the top and side CD is the bottom. They stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel. BC and AD meet AB at right angles.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: In B the lines stay the same distance apart and never meet. The lines in D get closer and would meet.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
items.e: The top and bottom are one pair. The left and right sides are another pair. That is 2 pairs.

items.q: Which side of this trapezoid is parallel to side AB?
items.e: The top AB and the bottom CD stay the same distance apart. Side BC is slanted and side AD is perpendicular to AB.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this trapezoid have?
items.e: Only the top and the bottom are parallel. The two slanted sides get closer at the top, so they would meet.

items.q: What are perpendicular lines?
c: lines that are the same length
lines that meet at a right angle
lines that meet at any angle
items.e: Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle, like the two edges at the corner of a page.

items.q: Olivia says these lines cannot be parallel because they are slanted. Is she right?
c: Yes, parallel lines must be flat
items.e: The lines stay the same distance apart all the way along, so they are parallel. Parallel lines can point in any direction.

items.q: Which pair is perpendicular?
c: the top and bottom edges of a door
the two rails of a train track
a flagpole and the flat ground
items.e: A flagpole stands straight up, so it meets the flat ground at a right angle. The other pairs are parallel.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: In C the lines meet at a square corner, so they are perpendicular. A tilted corner can still be a right angle.

items.q: In rectangle ABCD, how many sides are perpendicular to side AB?
items.e: Sides AD and BC each meet side AB at a right angle, so 2 sides are perpendicular to it. Side CD is parallel to AB.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: In D the slanted lines stay the same distance apart: they are parallel. Parallel lines do not have to be flat.

items.q: Emma says these lines are parallel because they do not touch. Is she right?
c: Yes, lines that do not touch are parallel
No, they get closer and would meet
items.e: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart. These lines get closer to the right, so they would meet if they were longer.

items.q: Mei says these lines are not perpendicular because neither line is straight up and down. Is she right?
c: No, they meet at a right angle, so they are perpendicular
Yes, one line must be straight up and down
items.e: Any two lines that meet at a right angle are perpendicular, even when both are tilted.

items.q: Which capital letter has a pair of parallel lines?
items.e: The two upright lines of H stay the same distance apart. T and L have lines that meet, and the lines of V meet at the bottom.

items.q: The two blue lines on a hockey rink go straight across the ice from one side to the other. They are always the same distance apart. How are the blue lines?
items.e: Lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet are parallel.

items.q: Which capital letter is made of 2 perpendicular lines?
items.e: The two lines of L meet at a square corner. The lines of V and X meet at angles that are not right angles, and H has 3 lines.

items.q: Two perpendicular lines cross. What kind of angles do they make?
items.e: Perpendicular lines meet at right angles. When they cross, they make 4 right angles.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: In A the lines cross and make 4 square corners. In B they cross, but not at a right angle.

items.q: What are parallel lines?
c: lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet
lines that meet at a right angle
items.e: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart, like the two rails of a train track.

sets.title: Rectangles and squares: right angles and symmetry

items.q: Lucas draws a shape with 4 sides. Every corner is a right angle and all 4 sides are 5 cm long. What is the best name for the shape?
items.e: 4 right angles and 4 equal sides make a square.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, the halves do not match when you fold on it
Yes, it goes from corner to corner
Yes, it cuts the rectangle into 2 equal triangles
Yes, every diagonal is a line of symmetry
items.e: The 2 triangles are the same size, but if you fold on the diagonal, the corners stick out and do not match. A diagonal of a rectangle that is not a square is not a line of symmetry.

items.q: Which shape is a rectangle?
items.e: Shape B has 4 right angles (the small squares show them). Shape A leans over like a pushed box: its sides are parallel, but its corners are not right angles.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, a square has only 2 lines of symmetry
No, diagonals are never lines of symmetry
No, the halves are different sizes
Yes, the two halves match when you fold on it
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal, so folding on a diagonal makes the two halves match exactly.

items.q: Ethan folds a sheet of Letter paper (about 28 cm by 22 cm). In how many different ways can he fold it so the two halves match exactly?
items.e: Letter paper is a rectangle that is not a square. It folds in half across the middle and up and down the middle. Folding on a diagonal does not work.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
items.e: One line goes across the middle and one goes up and down the middle. The diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

items.q: A classroom window is a rectangle 120 cm wide and 80 cm tall. Which of its sides are parallel?
c: the top and the left side
the top and bottom, and the left and right sides
items.e: A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides: the top and bottom, and the left and right sides.

items.q: Which is true for every rectangle?
c: It has 4 right angles and 2 pairs of parallel sides
It has only 1 pair of parallel sides
All 4 sides are the same length
items.e: Every rectangle has 4 right angles, and its opposite sides are parallel. Only squares have 4 equal sides and 4 lines of symmetry.

items.q: Is a square a rectangle?
c: Yes, it has 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel
No, a square has no parallel sides
No, a rectangle must have 2 long sides and 2 short sides
No, a square has no right angles
items.e: A rectangle is a shape with 4 sides and 4 right angles. A square has all of that, so it is a special rectangle with 4 equal sides.

items.q: Zoe builds a garden bed with 2 sides 2 m long and 2 sides 1 m long. The corners are not right angles. Is the garden bed a rectangle?
c: No, a rectangle needs 4 equal sides
No, a rectangle needs 4 right angles
Yes, opposite sides are the same length
items.e: Equal opposite sides are not enough. A rectangle must have 4 right angles.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
items.e: A square has 2 lines through the middles of the sides and 2 diagonals: 4 lines of symmetry.

items.q: Nathan says a rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry because it has 4 sides. Is he right?
c: No, a rectangle that is not a square has 2 lines of symmetry
No, a rectangle has no lines of symmetry
Yes, every shape with 4 sides has 4
No, a rectangle has 1 line of symmetry
items.e: Only the lines across the middle and up and down the middle fold a rectangle into matching halves. The diagonals do not.

items.q: A soccer field is a rectangle. Chloe runs along the side of the field, then turns at the corner flag to run along the goal line. What angle do the side line and the goal line make?
items.e: The corners of a rectangle are right angles, so the side line and the goal line meet at a right angle.

items.q: Aiden checks that a picture frame is a rectangle. What should he check at each corner?
c: that it is an acute angle
that it is a right angle
that it is a straight angle
that it is an obtuse angle
items.e: A rectangle has 4 right angles. Aiden can check each corner with the corner of a sheet of paper.

items.q: In which shape is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
items.e: Only the square folds exactly onto itself along its diagonal. The rectangle’s diagonal does not work, the line that is not in the middle makes 2 different parts, and the slanted shape does not match when folded.

items.q: A door is a rectangle. How do the side edge and the bottom edge of the door meet?
c: They are perpendicular: they make a right angle
items.e: Sides of a rectangle that meet at a corner make a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: The flag of Canada is a rectangle. It has a red band on each side and a red maple leaf in the middle. How many lines of symmetry does the flag have?
items.e: Fold the flag down the middle from top to bottom: the left and right halves match. Folding across the middle does not work, because the maple leaf is not the same at the top and the bottom.

items.q: Is the dashed line a line of symmetry?
c: No, only slanted lines can be lines of symmetry
Yes, the two halves match when you fold on it
No, a rectangle has no lines of symmetry
No, the halves are different sizes
items.e: Fold the rectangle on the dashed line. The top half lands exactly on the bottom half.

items.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
items.e: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner, so a rectangle has 4 right angles.

items.q: Mateo cuts out a square of paper to make an origami card. In how many different ways can he fold it so the two halves match exactly?
items.e: A square has 4 lines of symmetry: across the middle, up and down the middle, and the 2 diagonals.
